# Edmund S. Muskie Internship Program
The Edmund S. Muskie Internship Program is a professional exchange program supported by the United States Department of State, designed to provide summer internship placements, career training, and financial support to Eurasian scholars and graduate students studying in the United States. Established by the United States Congress in fiscal year 1992 (Pub. L. 102–138, Sec. 227) and named by the Freedom Support Act of 1992 (Pub. L. 102–511, Sec. 801), the program was originally administered by the International Research & Exchanges Board, the American Council of Teachers of Russian, and the American Council for Collaboration in Education and Language. In 2015, the program underwent a significant renewal, adopting a new format and scope and being launched by Cultural Vistas, marking a shift from its previous administrative structure.
The program focuses on fostering international collaboration and understanding through direct engagement with U.S. institutions, though the text does not specify the exact host universities or the specific countries of origin for the Eurasian scholars. The Muskie Internship Program operates as a distinct initiative within the broader landscape of international educational exchanges, distinct from other named programs such as the Kennedy Scholarship (which supports British students at Harvard and MIT), the Marshall Scholarship (for U.S. students in the UK), and the Fulbright Program (which facilitates bilateral exchanges between the U.S. and numerous other nations).
